items.reasons: A better preserves the existing meaning while carrying the operator’s convergence and compounding wording. The base template and harness defaults explicitly recognize the installed client as a source of truth. B retains the verification order, but checking something first does not explicitly preserve its authority when installed behavior differs from current upstream. A preserves both obligations and matches the agreed X5a opening apart from markup. This is a semantic judgment, not a demonstrated model-behavior result. I verified the packet hash, both resolutions’ hashes and counts, and all three changed-file registrations. Five focused tests passed in each tree through direct module imports, avoiding the package initializer’s temporary-directory writes. A’s 153-word block, 3371-byte template and required co-changes are consistent.
